messages:
maya: UX review — spend console layout idea: make the timeline the primary canvas, with each time slice row expandable to show a compact token breakdown + inline invoice preview. wireframe: https://redwood.app/s/tnl-wireframe :thinking_face:

darren: timeline-first is interesting. my worry: when you have 40 projects the vertical scan gets rough. do we lose quick totals?

sarah: agree with darren. must keep org total visible. suggest a sticky org header with 1-line totals and a project quick-search. also accessibility: sparkline colors need to meet contrast in dark mode.

kevin: +1 on sticky header. about the expanded breakdown — prefer collapsed by default and only expand for selected projects. also need an easy CSV / export per-row. CFO will want that.

maya: plan idea: default view = org rollup shown in sticky header. timeline-tab shows per-day rows. click a project name to jump to project-focused timeline. expanded row shows: top: token summary (text/embedding/rerank), middle: mini invoices (most recent), bottom: actions (download PDF, export CSV).

sarah: tiny copy nits: change "Download invoice" -> "Download PDF" (less ambiguous). invoice date format should be YYYY-MM-DD for sorting and voiceover clarity.

darren: performance note: rendering expanded token breakdown for ~100 rows will be heavy. suggest virtualization + only fetch token details on expand. add aria-live region for async updates.

kevin: + accessibility: ensure expand/collapse is keyboard focusable and uses `aria-expanded`. also provide an alt text for the sparkline like: "7-day spend sparkline, peak on 2026-02-15".

maya: agreed on lazy fetch. rough API sketch for preview (will mock with eng):

```
GET /api/v1/spend?view=timeline&project=proj_123&start=2026-02-01&end=2026-02-28
Response: {
  "summary_line": "Org total: $12,345",
  "rows": [ { "date": "2026-02-01", "tokens": {"text": 12000, "embed": 3400} } ]
}
```

kevin: minor: try to avoid returning huge token arrays in the row response. return a small summary + a `details_url` for on-demand fetch.

billing-bot: New invoice uploaded for org: rwd-98765 (2026-02-28) — https://billing.redwood/app/invoices/rwd-98765 :package:

sarah: cool — one more a11y point: for the inline invoice preview, ensure the download button has an aria-label that includes invoice number and amount, e.g. `aria-label="Download PDF invoice rwd-98765, $1,234.56"`. screenreader users otherwise lose context when tabbing through rows.

darren: layout suggestion: instead of fully inline invoices (which push content down), show a 1-line invoice summary with a chevron to open a right-side flyout for full invoice. flyout keeps vertical rhythm and reduces noise.

maya: good call. tradeoffs: inline reduces clicks for finance folks, flyout reduces noise and is more keyboard friendly. compromise: show 1 most-recent invoice inline, and a "View history" chevron that opens flyout. I'll mock this and return with updated frames.

kevin: UX QA checklist for the new mock:
- contrast check (light+dark)
- keyboard nav for expand/collapse and flyout
- aria labels for actions and sparklines
- export flow (CSV/PDF) per-row
- lazy-loading indicator for token details

sarah: also include tooltip copy for toggles: "Account-level view" vs "Project view" — keep it short. avoid jargon like "workspace" in the tooltip.

maya: thanks all — I'll update the Figma with two variants (inline-most-recent + flyout) and add a small prototype for keyboard interactions. aiming for a follow-up tomorrow EOD. :raised_hands:
